title.narrative: Continued cooperation between SwEPA and KEPA 2025-2027
Continued cooperation between SwEPA and KEPA 2025-2027

description.narrative:
The project is a continuation of the previous cooperation between the Kosovo Environmental Protection Agency, KEPA and the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency, SwEPA - which aims to pave the way for Kosovo to meet the environmental requirements to become a member of the EU. The title of the project is "Continued Cooperation between Swedish Environmental and Protection Agency - Capacity Building on Nature Protection and Environmental Data Use". The overall outcome of the project is "KEPA delivers its tasks regarding nature protection and environmental data in a more systematic, efficient and transparent way". Sida has shortened the new contribution's title to: Continued cooperation between SwEPA and KEPA 2025-2027.
Priority areas for the project are to improve data and measures when it comes to, for example, air quality, strengthened protection of national parks including biodiversity and preparation for KEPA to implement and monitor Natura 2000 areas. A red thread in the project is to build capacity for KEPA in order for the institution to strengthen its coordinating role in Kosovo for environmental data. The authority shall also lead planning and monitoring, and contribute to measures to improve the protection of Kosovo's national parks and Natura 2000 sites. Within the project, communication activities are integrated, not least to cooperate better with other actors and to reach out to the citizens. Data will be a core issue for KEPA; to improve, report and disseminate facts about the environment, which is needed for increased knowledge about the country's environmental situation and for decisions to take action.
Sida assesses that the project is well planned and has a results framework that matches the requirements for EU-accession, especially the EU Directive, Article 27, but also the EU Directive on Publicity (INSPIRE) and the EU's Habitat and Birds Directive and the Aarhus Convention. The project's priority areas are also in line with the recently approved national strategy: Kosovo Strategy for Environmental Protection 2024-2033. It is also in line with the Strategy for Sweden's Reform Cooperation with the Western Balkans and Turkey, 2021 to 2027.
At the global level, the project will contribute to Agenda 2030, as the project is in line with SDG 13, Climate Action, SDG 15 Life on Land and Goal 16, Peace, justice and strong institutions.

Detta projekt är en fortsättning på ett samarbete mellan Sveriges och Kosovos Naturvårdsverk. Baserat på deras tidigare fyra år (2020-2024) av samarbete kommer fokus för den fortsatta perioden att vara: 1) Att bygga en effektiv insamling, hantering och användning av miljödata. 2) Stärka planering, förvaltning och övervakning av skyddade områden i Kosovo. 3) Strukturera utvecklingen av Natura 2000-områden. This project is a continuation of a collaboration between Sweden's and Kosovo's agencies for Environmental and Protection. Based on their earlier four years (2020-2024) of collaboration the focus for the continued period will be: 1) Building an efficient collection, management and use of environmental data. 2) Strengthening the planning, management and monitoring of protected areas in Kosovo. 3) Structuring the development of Natura 2000 areas. The activities are in line with the EU-directives and will support Kosovo to become an EU-member.

In 2025, the cooperation mainly contributed to foundational but relevant changes at outcome level.
Public authorities involved in the environmental metadata portal developed a better understanding of, and greater acceptance for, a linked-data model. Under this approach, environmental information remains with the institutions that produce it but can still be connected and shared through a common system, rather than transferring ownership of all data to the Kosovo Environmental Protection Agency (KEPA). This is an important condition for wider environmental data sharing in the future.
Contacts between Kosovo, North Macedonia and Montenegro also became more structured, creating a stronger basis for future cross-border cooperation on protected areas.
Regarding preparations for Natura 2000, KEPA and other relevant institutions gained a clearer understanding of their respective roles, gaps in the existing reference lists and the requirements for further work. KEPA also approved a work plan to guide the continued preparation process.
Within KEPA, signed Memoranda of Understanding, appointed focal points and established working groups broadened institutional participation and reduced dependence on individual staff members.
An unexpected but useful development followed the hacking incident and the technical constraints identified by the Agency for Information Society. These challenges led to a more realistic technical approach that is better adapted to KEPAs available data and the capacity of existing information systems.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
